own_solution.law: At normal incidence, d sin(theta) = m lambda. The angular separation is [asin(m lambda2/d) - asin(m lambda1/d)] × 180/pi, using common length units.
assumptions: The usual ideal transmission-grating model applies.
The compared maxima have order 2 and lie on the same side of the central beam.

notes: All certified numerical answers agree with the grating equation: replacement wavelengths 490, 520 and 560 nm give separations 4.78374, 3.89551 and 2.70537 degrees, respectively. All listed wavelengths permit second-order maxima. Earlier measurements and light entering the separate spectrometer leave the present beam unchanged. Screen distance cancels through theta = atan(y/L), with y = L tan(theta), for every listed positive distance. Lengths must be converted to common units and inverse-trigonometric results converted to degrees.
